newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC cuts wheat, barley, maize stocks forecasts.
newsitem.headline: ONIC cuts wheat, barley, maize stocks forecasts.

text.p: France's grain office ONIC confirmed on Wednesday it had lowered its estimates for closing soft wheat, barley and maize stocks.

In a new supply/demand report released ahead of ONIC's monthly news conference, the office cut its forecast for the 1996/97 barley carryover to 905,000 tonnes from a previous estimate of 1.045 million tonnes. This would compare with a carryover of 626,000 tonnes at end June 1996.
This partly followed an increase in off-farm consumption on the domestic market to 1.635 million tonnes from 1.585 million forecast last month.
ONIC also raised barley exports to European Union countries to 2.37 million tonnes from a previous target of 2.28 million tonnes. It kept its non-EU export goal unchanged at 1.5 million tonnes.
Barley production rose last year to a revised 9.497 million tonnes from 7.739 million in 1995.

ONIC also slightly cut its estimate for closing soft wheat stocks to 2.021 million tonnes from a previous target of 2.061 million tonnes. This would compare with soft wheat stocks of 2.212 million tonnes at end June 1996.

ONIC kept its target for soft wheat exports to non-EU countries unchanged at 6.4 million tonnes but raised its target for exports to European Union countries to 9.185 million tonnes from a previous estimate of 9.135 million tonnes.
Soft wheat production was revised up to 34.657 million tonnes from 34.578 million tonnes. This would compare with a 1995 harvest of 29.825 million tonnes.
ONIC cut is estimate for closing maize stocks to 2.479 million tonnes from 2.519 million last month. This would compare with closing stocks of 1.647 million tonnes at end June 1996.
It raised its goal for exports within the European Union to 6.535 million tonnes from 6.435 million tonnes last month.
It put the 1996 maize harvest at 14.304 million tonnes, up slightly from 14.280 million forecast last month. This would compare with a 1995 crop of 12.394 million tonnes.
